title: AUTOMATED CONCEPT DISCOVERY FOR LLM-AS-A JUDGE PREFERENCE ANALYSIS

bias_targets.methodology: Calculating the preference rate for the second response (Response B) in randomized paired evaluations to identify statistically significant deviations from an expected 50% baseline.
Measuring the rate at which an LLM judge (e.g., GPT-5.1) prefers responses generated by models from its own provider compared to human preference baselines.

Extracting latent preference features using Differential Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) and calculating length-controlled delta win-rates to show LLMs prefer refusing sensitive requests at higher rates than humans.

Applying automated concept extraction on domain-specific datasets (e.g., askacademia) to discover and measure LLM judges' systematic preference for longer, more detailed, and more formal responses compared to human judges.

Training Differential SAEs on response embedding differences to automatically discover and evaluate previously unknown content biases, such as LLMs favoring concreteness, empathy, and formal procedural advice over flexibility, personal growth, and self-directed actions.
